scenes.say: Ever wondered what pods actually are in Kubernetes? Why are they the foundation for everything else?

scenes.label: Pod
scenes.sub: Smallest unit in Kubernetes. Holds one or more containers.
scenes.say: A pod is the smallest unit in Kubernetes. It can hold one or more containers, grouped together.
Pods share an IP address, storage volumes, and always run together on the same node. They're disposable—Kubernetes replaces them as needed.

scenes.title: Pod creation & inspection
scenes.say: You can create a pod with a simple YAML file and check its details with a command. But in practice, deployments handle pod creation for you.

scenes.question: Is a pod just a container?
scenes.right: No, a pod wraps one or more containers. It shares network and storage, and is managed as a unit.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: Is a pod just a container? No, a pod wraps one or more containers, sharing network and storage.
